amendment: 19 Aug 2026: version 4 removes the LINE_MANAGER step. Desicon has ONE approval before Cost Control -- the Head of Department -- confirmed against the list of requesting accounts and their approvers. Version 3 modelled two, a line manager and then a department head, which for Desicon would have meant the same person approving the same request twice. Two clicks for one judgement teaches people that a step is ceremony, and a step people treat as ceremony is not a control. No version 3 file is retained because the database was reset for UAT and nothing was ever pinned to it; the next change after UAT begins must keep its predecessor. See docs/15 section 3.
note: Version 3 splits FinanceOfficer into CostControlOfficer and TreasuryOfficer. Version 2 recorded that Cost Control and the Accounts Officer who posts in Business Central were the same people; they are not. They are separate desks with separate mailboxes (costcontrol@ and treasury@), and one role covering both meant a single person could verify the costing, post it, and execute the payment -- with the posting notification going to the wrong desk, so the person who had to act was never told. Version 2 remains published for requests already open under it; see expense-reimbursement.v2.workflow.json and docs/15-Go-Live-Checklist.md section 3.

policyValues.note: Above this net payable amount, payment is by bank transfer to the employee account. Source: DEL-AC-FRM-002 Rev 05 footer. Confirm current figure with Finance. A future rate change is a new row here with a later effectiveFrom, not an edit to this one -- see WorkflowDefinitionExtensions.GetPolicyValue.

transitions.guardMessage: Add at least one expense line and attach receipts before submitting.
transitions.note: Straight to the Head of Department. Version 3 routed through a line manager first; Desicon has one approval on the requesting side, and modelling two meant the same person approving twice.

transitions.guardMessage: You cannot approve your own request.
transitions.note: Final approval on the requesting side. Everything after this happens inside Accounts.

transitions.guardMessage: Receipts must be complete, at least one receipt attached, and a Treasury number captured before this proceeds.
transitions.note: Cost Control checks that the claim is costed to the right centre. A separate desk from the Treasury officer who posts it at AWAITING_POSTING -- version 2 modelled them as one role, which let the same person check the costing and then post against their own check.

transitions.guardMessage: Return is available when receipts are marked Incomplete.
transitions.note: The 'Incomplete' tick on the paper form maps to a return, not a rejection.

transitions.guardMessage: You cannot approve your own claim.
transitions.note: The Accounts Manager. Releases the claim for treatment, but does not release money -- that is the Director of Finance's alone. Only claims that actually pay someone go that way; see the two sibling branches.

transitions.guardMessage: You cannot approve your own claim.
transitions.note: A retirement that exactly matched the advance. Nothing is paid and nothing is refunded, so the Director of Finance's gate does not apply -- it exists to authorise money leaving, and no money leaves. It still has to reach BC, hence AWAITING_POSTING rather than straight to CLOSED.

transitions.guardMessage: This branch applies only when the advance exceeded the amount spent.
transitions.note: Employee spent less than the advance taken and owes the difference back. Money comes in rather than going out, so this branch bypasses the DMD too.

transitions.guardMessage: The refund received must equal the amount over-drawn.
transitions.note: The Accounts Manager confirms the refund, as on the retirement form -- whether money is owed to the employee or back to the company, it is the same person's call. Goes straight to posting: the Director of Finance authorises money leaving, and this is money arriving.

The negative path the validator flagged as missing, and it was missing in version 1 too. Without it, a claim where the employee never pays back the over-drawn amount has exactly one exit -- CONFIRM_REFUND -- whose guard requires the refund to have been received. An employee who simply does not pay leaves the request parked in REFUND_DUE with no action available to anybody, which is how a debt becomes invisible rather than collected.

transitions.guardMessage: You cannot approve payment of your own claim.
transitions.note: The gate. No money moves at Desicon without the Director of Finance, and version 1 of this definition did not have it at all -- payment was executable by the Accounts Officer on the Accounts Manager's approval alone. Placed before posting because the DMD authorises the payment decision and the BC entry is the execution of it.

transitions.guardMessage: Enter the Business Central document number for this posting.
transitions.note: The Accounts Officer posts in Business Central, then records here that she has and under which document number. This platform deliberately captures no journal lines: BC owns the ledger, and a second copy of the same journal in a different system is two versions of the truth waiting to disagree. The document number is the only key tying this approval trail to the ledger entry, which is why it is required rather than optional.

transitions.guardMessage: Enter the Business Central document number for this posting.
transitions.note: A retirement that paid nobody -- balanced exactly, or refunded to the company. Once BC has it there is nothing to pay and nothing for a recipient to acknowledge, so it closes here. Routing it through AWAITING_PAYMENT would leave a claim sitting in the Accounts Officer's payment queue forever with nothing to pay, which is how a queue stops being believed.

transitions.guardMessage: A bank transfer requires the beneficiary to have bank details on file, and whoever last set those details cannot be the person who pays against them.
transitions.note: PaymentMethod is derived by ExpenseRequest.ApplyPaymentMethodPolicy at submission/recalculation time, not captured here -- Finance cannot choose it at payment execution. The bank-details clauses moved here from version 1's AUTHORISE transition, which no longer exists; they guard the moment money actually leaves, which is where they belong.

Only the beneficiary can close the request. Finance marking it paid is not sufficient. This step is not in the paper process, which is precisely why claims could sit marked-paid and unreceived for eighteen months.
The beneficiary disputes receipt. Returns the item to Finance with the dispute recorded.
